questions.q: What is the out-of-box default for max server memory, and why is that a problem?
options: Effectively unlimited — the Database Engine will consume RAM until the OS is starved
It defaults to 4 GB, which is too low for most servers
It defaults to exactly half of installed RAM
It cannot be changed once set during Setup
questions.explain: Left unset, the Engine will take memory the OS and any co-hosted services need, which is why setting it explicitly is a standard post-install step.

questions.q: Why is the default value of 5 for cost threshold for parallelism considered a problem on modern hardware?
options: It was set decades ago for far older hardware and is too low, causing small, cheap queries to go parallel unnecessarily
It disables parallelism entirely on all modern servers
It only affects backup operations, not queries
SQL Server ignores this setting on any server with more than 8 cores
questions.explain: Raising cost threshold for parallelism to roughly 25-50 is common practice on modern hardware to avoid unnecessary parallel plans for cheap queries.

questions.q: Why does tempdb's default single data file cause contention?
options: Every session on the instance can use tempdb concurrently, causing allocation page contention on a single file
A single tempdb file is not allowed to grow automatically
Single-file tempdb only affects Analysis Services, not the Database Engine
It has no real effect — file count never matters for tempdb
questions.explain: With a single file, concurrent sessions contend on allocation pages like PFS/GAM/SGAM; multiple equally-sized files spread that contention out.

questions.q: Why must tempdb's multiple data files be kept equally sized?
options: SQL Server's proportional-fill algorithm allocates more heavily to larger files, defeating the purpose of splitting them
Unequal file sizes cause SQL Server to refuse to start
Only the first tempdb file is ever used; the rest are purely for backup redundancy
Equal sizing is only a cosmetic best practice with no functional effect
questions.explain: If files drift apart in size, proportional fill sends disproportionately more allocations to the larger files, undoing the benefit of multiple files.

questions.q: What does turning on backup compression default actually change?
options: New backups are compressed by default without needing WITH COMPRESSION on every BACKUP statement
It compresses the transaction log automatically on every write
It changes the collation used for backup metadata
It disables the ability to take uncompressed backups entirely
questions.explain: backup compression default makes compression the default behavior for new backups, typically producing smaller, often faster backups at the cost of more CPU during the operation.
